ADVISORY_BODY: Today reversed Tuesday's record-chasing mood without breaking anything structurally: the S&P 500 fell as much as -0.71% intraday before closing just -0.22% at 7,801.77, and the Nasdaq Composite closed -0.22% at 27,538.69 after also pulling back from Tuesday's fresh high of 27,599.79. The Dow fell -0.66% to 51,179.87 and the Russell 2000 led losses at -1.31% to 2,793.20 — small-caps remain the weakest link in this tape for a second straight session. The proximate trigger was the bond market: the 10-Year Treasury yield spiked to 5.364% intraday, a fresh 24-year high, after the FOMC's Sept 15-16 minutes showed every participant backed that meeting's quarter-point hike and most officials now expect another increase before year-end, timing split between the Oct 28 and Dec 9 meetings (Chair Warsh called the September move removal of a 'dose of accommodation'). What pulled the tape off its lows was a genuinely strong $39 billion 10-year note auction: it stopped out at 5.300% — the highest 10-year auction yield since November 2000, and 1.7bp through the when-issued level — on a 2.77x bid-to-cover (vs. a 2.51x trailing average) and 80.3% foreign/indirect demand (vs. roughly 71.5% average), pulling the 10Y back to about 5.277% by the close. Markets still price only about 16-17% odds of a hike at the Oct 28 FOMC (82-84% hold), essentially unchanged from Monday. The breadth picture is genuinely counter-intuitive today: a Nasdaq post-close screen (ts2.tech) showed 3,283 advancers against 3,187 decliners across 6,992 securities — roughly balanced, slightly positive — meaning today's index-level decline was a mega-cap-concentration story in reverse of the 'narrow rally' pattern flagged in recent sessions: a handful of large names dragged the cap-weighted indexes down while the median stock was closer to flat. Sector-wise, FMP's NASDAQ-listed snapshot shows Utilities (+2.26%) and Technology (+1.14%) still working, while Real Estate (-1.12%), Basic Materials (-1.04%) and Energy (-0.94%) lagged; a broader S&P 500 sector-ETF cross-check (ts2.tech) tells a harsher story for cyclicals specifically — Industrials -2.18% (Caterpillar -5.75% on a downgrade, Deere -3.80%) and Materials -1.51% (Worthington Steel -6.89% on weaker results), with Health Care the lone S&P sector gainer (+1.03%, Eli Lilly +2.70%). The one operational note that matters most for today's futures-level work: Schwab's /ES and /NQ feed has now failed with an HTTP 400 error on every attempt for a third consecutive session (Mon 10/5, Tue 10/6, and today), and the FMP cash-index fallback has not populated either contract on any of those three days — there are no real settlement, pivot, or value-area numbers for /ES or /NQ today, and the Analysis/Trade Idea/Levels boxes below say so plainly rather than inventing any. Analysis
Today's calendar carried two real catalysts: the FOMC's Sept 15-16 meeting minutes at 2:00 PM ET, and a $39 billion 10-year Treasury note auction. The minutes showed every participant backed September's quarter-point hike and most now expect another increase before year-end, with timing split between the Oct 28 and Dec 9 meetings — Chair Warsh described the hike as removing a 'dose of accommodation.' The auction was the session's real surprise: it stopped out at 5.300% (the highest 10-year auction yield since November 2000) on a 2.77x bid-to-cover (vs. a 2.51x trailing average) and 80.3% foreign/indirect demand (vs. roughly 71.5% average) — genuinely strong demand at a 24-year-high yield, which pulled the 10Y back from its intraday peak of 5.364% to roughly 5.277% by the close and helped equities recover more than half their intraday loss.
Spec. Move
A weak follow-through on Fed-speak tomorrow, or a soft reception to Thursday's PepsiCo/Tilray earnings, could reopen today's yield-driven selloff. A continued retreat in the 10Y toward 5.20% or below would be the cleaner signal that today's auction result, not just the hawkish minutes, is what the market ends up pricing.
Trade Idea
No pre-positioning into the next session on this calendar alone — today's auction result is the stronger signal than the minutes themselves, and it's already in the tape. Watch whether the 10Y holds its post-auction retreat tomorrow.
